title: host.v1: every message between the daemon and a plugin host ('csl-plugin-host/1')
description: One channel per loaded plugin; every load on a channel names the plugin the channel was opened for. This file holds every message on it. A plugin's whole world is the messages on its one channel to the daemon: the plugin imports nothing from Recursion and shares no object with the daemon. FRAMING: the length-prefixed frames of control_transport/framing.py, reused as they are: a 4-byte big-endian length, then that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON holding one object. FRAME SIZE: a load frame (daemon to host only) may be as large as the daemon's largest package needs: the daemon's largest manifest and largest package file (MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES and MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES of plugin_security/limits.py, the sizes daemon/plugins.py reads) as base64, plus the load's envelope with the longest plugin id; that limit is computed from those constants, never a second number. Every other frame, and every frame a host sends, is at most 1 MiB. A package that still does not fit one load frame is refused on the daemon's side with 'load_too_large' and is never sent; it is never a frame error. The daemon's side also holds the package sizes itself: a manifest over MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES or a package file over MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES is refused 'load_too_large' before any frame is built. No load comes in parts in this release. Every byte string on the channel is standard base64 with padding, in a field whose name ends in '_b64'. THE MESSAGES (each in $defs): hello (each side sends it once, first; a second hello is refused 'message_invalid'; the two ends of plugin_security/host_channel.py make no other message wait for it, and a program above an end may); load (daemon to host: one plugin's id, its manifest bytes and its verified package files as bytes; load may arrive after hello at any time, even though the daemon sends it only at start in this release); call (either side: a call NAME taken from the one append-only list x-call-names, with its arguments; defined both ways: the daemon is to call a plugin's function by name, and a plugin's host calls a broker handle by name; at this head the daemon's end sends no call: the daemon's own call of a plugin's function through this channel is later work, and until it is built daemon/plugins.py calls those functions in its own process); core (host to daemon: one csl-core/v0 request, its bytes unchanged; daemon to host: the core's answer, its bytes unchanged); result (either side: what a call returned, under the id of the call it answers; a result for an id the receiver never called is refused); refusal (each side: a typed refusal of one message); bye (each side, at any time, also before the hello: the channel ends; after a bye every later message is refused 'message_invalid' and the end that took it sends nothing more). THE CALLER: the daemon sets the caller of every core message from the channel it came in on, never from the message: no message carries a caller, and a core message that names one is refused 'caller_forged' before the core sees it. Every csl-core/v0 op stays the core's: the host relays the bytes and decides nothing, and every call still passes the core's one dispatcher. CALL NAMES: x-call-names is ONE list, append-only, never a fixed set of message types: a later surface kind is a new name on that list and never a schema break. A call whose name the receiver does not know is refused 'call_unknown' and nothing runs; a call with a reserved name is refused 'call_reserved' with the words 'reserved; not available in this release' and nothing runs; at the daemon that refusal comes before any other check of the name. MESSAGE TYPES: a message whose type the receiver does not know is answered with a typed refusal ('message_unknown') and the channel stays up; the message names in x-reserved.message_types are reserved: named here, refused 'message_reserved' if sent in this release, never built here. x-refusal-codes lists each code this channel answers with; an end makes a refusal only with one of them. A refusal that arrives with a code not on that list is still read as a refusal of the message its id names: a newer peer may know a newer code, and the list is append-only. THE ROOT: a message is valid at the root of this file when it is one of the seven message forms in $defs (oneOf); each form fixes its own type, so the message's type decides which form applies, and a message of any other type is refused at the root as the receiver refuses it.

x-call-names.name: registry
x-call-names.about: The plugin's panels for the page, as registry() returns them today.

x-call-names.name: operator
x-call-names.about: One o7.operator.v0 read command; the daemon keeps its own deadline on the answer.

x-call-names.name: surfaces
x-call-names.about: The surfaces a plugin offers (provisional: no host calls it on master).

x-call-names.name: surface
x-call-names.about: One surface by kind and name (provisional: no host calls it on master).

x-reserved.about: Names reserved for later work. Each is answered as reserved, with the words 'reserved; not available in this release', and nothing is built for it here: no handler, no permission that grants anything, no record writer. These lists are append-only. Reserved is not frozen: a reserved name may be corrected until the first build that answers it. When it is built, each reserved call name here is sent by a plugin's host to the daemon (the plugin asks the core: run.request for a run, the computer names for a computer or browser session, net.request and net.connect for the network) and answered by result or refusal; that is why call and result travel both ways.

call_names.name: run.request
call_names.about: A plugin asks for a run it owns; no run is started by this channel in this release.

call_names.name: computer.open
call_names.about: Opens a computer or browser session for a plugin.

call_names.name: computer.act
call_names.about: One action in an open computer or browser session.

call_names.name: computer.observe
call_names.about: What an open computer or browser session shows now.

call_names.name: computer.close
call_names.about: Ends a computer or browser session.

call_names.name: net.request
call_names.about: The core makes an HTTPS request to a granted destination and returns the answer.

call_names.name: net.connect
call_names.about: The core connects to a granted destination and hands the connected socket to the host.

message_types.name: event
message_types.about: An event delivered to a host that subscribed to it.

message_types.name: guard
message_types.about: An ask-or-deny round trip with a deadline.

message_types.name: surface.update
message_types.about: A surface update the host starts.

run_origin.name: trigger
run_origin.about: A run started by a scheduled task or another trigger.

run_origin.name: agent
run_origin.about: A run started by a persistent agent.

run_origin.name: packet
run_origin.about: A run started by a work packet from another node.

x-reserved.run_origin_about: Where a run came from. No message on this channel carries a run's origin yet, so no field is made for it: the three values are reserved here by name, and their refusal is placed when a field carries them.

x-inventory.about: Every function daemon/plugins.py calls on a plugin, and the one message that is to carry it once the daemon calls through this channel: at this head the daemon's end sends no call, and the daemon's own call through the channel is later work. registry, operator and bind_core are what daemon/plugins.py calls today, in the daemon's own process; surfaces and surface are the provisional ones of the themes plugin.

x-refusal-codes.message_invalid: The message is not one object of a known type with exactly its fields and their forms, or it is a result for an id the receiver never called, or it came after a bye, or it is a second hello.
x-refusal-codes.message_unknown: The receiver does not know the message type; the channel stays up.
x-refusal-codes.message_reserved: The message type is reserved; not available in this release. The channel stays up.
x-refusal-codes.message_wrong_side: The message type is known but is never sent by this side of the channel.
x-refusal-codes.caller_forged: A core message named a caller; the caller is set from the channel, so nothing reached the core.
x-refusal-codes.call_unknown: The receiver does not know the call name; nothing ran.
x-refusal-codes.call_reserved: The call name is reserved; not available in this release. Nothing ran.
x-refusal-codes.call_args_invalid: The call's arguments are not exactly the ones listed for its name; nothing ran.
x-refusal-codes.call_not_offered: The plugin does not offer this call; nothing ran.
x-refusal-codes.call_failed: The plugin's function raised (the detail names the exception's type only), tried to end the host process (SystemExit: the detail says so, and the host goes on), or returned a value that cannot be written as JSON (the detail names the value's type).
x-refusal-codes.load_too_large: The daemon's side: a manifest or a package file is over its size, or a package does not fit one load frame, so no load is sent; never a frame error.

id.description: A message id, chosen by the side that sends the request and echoed by the answer. A whole number written without a fraction: 1, never 1.0. JSON Schema cannot decide this (to it 1.0 is the integer 1), so a validator of this file accepts 1.0, and both ends refuse it 'message_invalid'.

bytes.description: Bytes as standard base64 with padding.

call_name.description: A name on the one append-only list x-call-names, or a reserved one, or one this receiver does not know: lower-case dotted words.

hello.description: The first message each side sends, naming the channel's version. Each side sends it once; a second hello is refused 'message_invalid'. The two ends of plugin_security/host_channel.py make no other message wait for it; a program above an end may.

load.description: Daemon to host: one plugin to load, as bytes the daemon has already verified; it names the plugin the channel was opened for, and one load frame may be as large as the daemon's largest package needs. load may arrive after hello at any time, even though the daemon sends it only at start in this release.

files.description: Every verified file of the package: its path inside the package and its bytes.

call.description: Either side: one call by NAME (the daemon is to call a plugin's function, which is later work: at this head the daemon's end sends no call; a plugin's host calls a broker handle). Which arguments a name takes is listed for it in x-call-names; the receiver refuses any other set.

args.description: The call's arguments by name; each value is the argument's own data.

additionalProperties.description: One argument's value, as the call's name defines it.

core.description: One csl-core/v0 request (host to daemon) or answer (daemon to host), its bytes unchanged. It carries no caller: the daemon sets the caller from the channel.

result.description: Either side: what one call returned, under the call's id. A result for an id the receiver never called is refused.

value.description: The plugin's own return value, as plain JSON.

refusal.description: Either side: a typed refusal of one message. id is the refused message's id, or null when it had none that could be read.

code.description: One of x-refusal-codes when an end of this release makes the refusal. A receiver reads any code of this form as a refusal: a newer peer may know a newer code.

bye.description: Either side, at any time, also before the hello: the channel ends. After a bye every later message is refused 'message_invalid', and the end that took it sends nothing more.
